findings.title: The emoji resize job calls `downsize` with five arguments, which matches no method, so every custom emoji upload's resize job raises
findings.description: `resize_emoji.rb:14` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`. The diff adds a second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at `optimized_image.rb:149`. Ruby does not overload by arity, so that definition replaces the five-parameter `downsize` at `optimized_image.rb:145`. The surviving method accepts at most four arguments, so the call raises `ArgumentError` when the job runs. The load-time definition raises nothing, so the failure appears only at runtime. The job is enqueued for every custom emoji upload by `Emoji.create_for` (`app/models/emoji.rb:73`). Each emoji therefore keeps its original dimensions instead of being capped at 100×100. Fix: restore the five-argument form for the emoji caller and remove the duplicate definition.

findings.title: API URL images over 10 MB are silently truncated, then shrunk and stored as if complete
findings.description: `uploads_controller.rb:55` now downloads with a fixed `10.megabytes` cap instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. `FileHelper.download` (`lib/file_helper.rb:18-20`) stops reading once the file exceeds the cap, but it neither raises nor reports the truncation. A remote image larger than 10 MB therefore arrives as its first ~10–10.5 MB. Before this diff the cap was `max_image_size_kb`, so the truncated file was always over the limit and `UploadValidator#maximum_image_file_size` (`lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:84`) rejected it. Now the new block at `uploads_controller.rb:63-70` shrinks the truncated file with up to five `OptimizedImage.downsize` calls and only then validates it. If ImageMagick accepts the truncated input and exits 0, which it typically does for a truncated JPEG with a warning, the damaged image is stored and the client gets a success response. I did not run ImageMagick, so the storing step depends on that behavior; the truncation itself is certain. The hard-coded cap also means `max_image_size_kb` values above 10 MB are no longer honored for URL uploads. Fix: detect truncation in `FileHelper.download` and reject it, and use the site setting as the cap.

findings.title: The client-side size check hard-codes 10 MB and ignores the per-type settings, so an existing test now fails
findings.description: `validateUploadedFile` replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with `10 * 1024`. The existing test "prevents files that are too big from being uploaded" (`test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6:52-61`) sets `max_image_size_kb = 5`, passes a 10 KB image, and expects rejection with `max_size_kb: 5`. With this change, 10 is not greater than 10240, so validation passes and both assertions fail. For attachments the client no longer checks `max_attachment_size_kb` at all. The server still enforces it, but an attachment over 10 MB is reported as "max 10240 KB" even when the real limit is lower. I traced this by hand and did not run the JS suite. Either the test should be updated to the new behavior, or the per-type limit should stay.

findings.title: The 413 error message hard-codes 10 MB instead of the deployment's configured limit
findings.description: On HTTP 413, `displayErrorForUpload` now tells the user the limit is 10 MB (`var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024`). A 413 comes from the web server, whose `client_max_body_size` the admin configures. The `max_image_size_kb` description (`config/locales/server.en.yml:1037`) says it must match that setting. The previous code showed `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. For any deployment where the web server limit is not 10 MB, the message names the wrong limit.

findings.title: A failed `downsize` conversion is neither logged nor reported, so the user gets a misleading "too large" error
findings.description: The loop at `uploads_controller.rb:66-69` ignores the boolean that `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns. `convert_with` (`optimized_image.rb:160-163`) returns `false` on a non-zero ImageMagick exit without logging. Only its `rescue` branch logs, and ImageMagick's stderr goes to `/dev/null` (`optimized_image.rb:161`). When conversion fails, for example on a corrupt `.png`, the loop retries five times silently. The validator then reports "image too large", which gives the user the wrong reason and leaves no trace in the logs. Fix: check the return value, log the failure, and surface a conversion error.

findings.title: Animated GIF handling depends on the temp file path ending in `.GIF`, which multipart uploads may not have
findings.description: `OptimizedImage.optimize` takes the animated path only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` (`optimized_image.rb:155`). The controller passes `tempfile.path` as `from`, not the upload's filename. For multipart uploads that path is Rack's temp file. The repo pins Rack 1.5.5 (`Gemfile.lock:231`), and I believe that version names temp files `RackMultipart…` with no extension. I could not open the Rack source in this environment to confirm. If the name has no extension, `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` has no effect on oversized uploads. `downsize_instructions` then takes only the first frame (`[0]`), so an animated GIF is flattened to one frame. Fix: give the temp file the original extension, or base the animation check on `filename`.
